title: sre-weekly-ops-sync-notes-2026-03-04
content:
Weekly SRE Ops Sync - notes & prep
Date: 2026-03-04
Owner: Alex Johnson
Attendees (expected): Alex Johnson, Priya Patel, Miguel Santos, Rina Chen, on-call rotation

Purpose:
- Quick review of SLOs and trends
- Paging analysis and noise reduction progress
- Top incidents review + RCA snippets
- Action items and owners for next week

1) SLOs / Health summary (TL;DR)
- Overall error-rate SLO (api-error-rate < 0.5%) - 7d avg currently 0.62% (regression vs 0.45% two weeks ago).
- P99 latency (user-facing generation) - target < 350ms, 7d p99 = 420ms (spike correlates with model-serving throttles during peak).
- Availability SLO (all regions) - 99.95% current month-to-date.

Notes:
- Error rate increase seems concentrated in EU region (eu-west-1) between 09:00-11:00 UTC. Possible correlation with autoscaler config change (see incident below).
- Latency increase tied to a backend dependency (kv-store) degradation and the recent kernel change in runtime that reduced batching headroom.

Metrics to bring next meeting:
- Per-region error-rate + top 5 endpoints producing errors
- P99 by route + breakdown by backend (kv-store, model-runtime, edge-proxy)

2) Paging trends / Alert noise
- Pager volume last 7 days: 38 pages (baseline 22). Increase due to two sources: (1) repeated kv-store timeouts (15 pages), (2) flaky canary alert firing for model A after rollout (8 pages).
- On-call feedback: alert thresholds too tight for transient kv-store spikes; some alert duplicates (edge-proxy and model-runtime alerts firing for same underlying issue).

Quick action suggestions:
- Add a 60s grouping window for kv-store timeout alerts to reduce duplicate paging. (See action 1)
- Triage canary alert to see if it should be converted to a warning (non-paging) until rollout stabilizes. (See action 2)

3) Top incidents since last sync
- INC-2026-03-01: EU autoscaler misconfiguration - root cause: bad deploy of autoscaler policy that reduced max burst. Impact: degraded throughput for dedicated clusters in eu-west-1 for ~45 minutes. Mitigation: rollback to previous autoscaler config. RCA in progress.
- INC-2026-02-27: kv-store transient network errors - root cause: flaky NIC driver on a subset of infra hosts. Impact: increased latency and errors for model infer calls. Mitigation: host replacement and coord with infra to pin driver version.

RCA status / follow-ups:
- Autoscaler incident: Priya leading full RCA doc; draft expected by 2026-03-06. Need to include checklist for staging validation of autoscaler policies.
- KV-store incident: Miguel coordinating kernel/driver patch and rolling repro strategy. Confirmed mitigations staged; schedule maintenance window next Tue.

4) Runbook / Playbook gaps identified
- No runbook for autoscaler rollout validation - we need a step-by-step pre-deploy checklist (canary plan + traffic shaping + rollback test).
- Runbook for kv-store degraded network behavior needs clearer host replacement steps and post-replace validation.

5) Action items (owner - due)
- Action 1: Add 60s grouping to kv-store timeout alerts and de-duplicate overlapping alerts. Owner: Alex Johnson - Due: 2026-03-06. Linked ticket: SRE-4821.
- Action 2: Change model-A canary alert to non-paging warning until rollout stabilizes; add a dashboard panel for canary health. Owner: Rina Chen - Due: 2026-03-05.
- Action 3: Autoscaler RCA draft and staging validation checklist. Owner: Priya Patel - Due: 2026-03-06.
- Action 4: Schedule kernel/driver maintenance for affected infra hosts; confirm rollback plan and post-maint validation. Owner: Miguel Santos - Due: 2026-03-09.
- Action 5: Create autoscaler pre-deploy runbook (short-form). Owner: Alex Johnson + Priya Patel - Due: 2026-03-10.

6) Meeting prep (what to bring)
- Priya: autoscaler config diffs and canary metrics snapshot
- Miguel: kv-store incident timeline + infra host list for maintenance
- Rina: model-A canary alert rule + recent canary evaluation results
- Alex: consolidated SLO dashboard links and proposed alert grouping patch (PR link)

7) Open questions / decisions required
- Do we move canary alerts to non-paging by default during first 48h of any rollout? Pros: reduces pager noise. Cons: could delay detection of regressions. Need to decide policy.
- Should we add an explicit pre-deploy autoscaler policy test in CI? Feasible: run small traffic generator in staging and assert throughput within expected bounds.

8) Notes to self / follow-ups after meeting
- Pull per-route error-rate list before meeting and annotate top 10 by volume
- Create GitHub PR for alert grouping change and request quick review from on-call
- Block 30m with infra for maintenance window planning (use internal calendar slot: infra-maint-2026-03-09)

Next sync goal:
- Bring SLOs back under the threshold for error-rate (target 0.5%) and reduce weekly pager volume by 30% via alert tuning and runbook improvements.

End of notes.
